title: CuCD-ID cross-testbed transferability and oracle-alarm response portability

research_questions.RQ1: Can a CuCD-ID record instantiate the frozen recovery selector inputs without fabricating unavailable mission, authorization, trust, freshness, contradiction, epoch, or completeness state?
research_questions.RQ2: Which external CuCD-ID attack classes have direct, conceptual, or no correspondence to the frozen event/evidence taxonomy?
research_questions.RQ3: When the externally supplied scenario label is used only as an offline oracle alarm, do frozen response-policy decisions remain invariant to attack subtype under identical recovery-evidence context?

oracle_alarm_rule: security_signal = (published scenario label != NORMAL); label is offline adjudication for this bridge and is not treated as a detector output or as a CuCD-ID policy-visible feature
interpretation_guards: Study 5 does not estimate CuCD-ID intrusion-detection accuracy or recall.
Study 5 does not claim that P0-P7 or Study-2 policies were executed on CuCD-ID packet rows.
The CuCD-ID class label is used only as an offline oracle alarm in the portability subtest.
Dataset class counts are construction counts and are not attack-prevalence weights.
No mission/contact/trust input is imputed from CuCD-ID telemetry features.
Studies 1-4 remain frozen and are not pooled with Study 5.
No operational spacecraft, RF, real credential, or third-party target is involved.
